symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A derived embedding table's catalog key_column records the ORIGIN column its _row_id values actually came from, so a reader can follow the provenance by joining source.<key_column> = derived._row_id. key_column is provenance only — the physical key of every embedding table is invariantly _row_id (jammi-db/src/store/mod.rs::EmbeddingTableSpec, ::materialize_embedding_table), and _row_id holds the source key's values.
symptom_spec.observable: propagate_embeddings and materialize_context recorded the literal key_column="_row_id" instead of the source's origin column. Over a source keyed by a real column (e.g. paper_id) with NO _row_id column, propagate -> the derived table records Some("_row_id") not Some("paper_id"). The catalog auto-resolvers then interpolate that name into a scan of the RAW source: filter_keys_by_split and hydrate_value_columns (jammi-ai/src/pipeline/context_set.rs) issue SELECT arrow_cast("_row_id",'Utf8') FROM <raw source> and fail 'Schema error: No field named _row_id'. Reached end-to-end by train_context_predictor, which builds ContextRequest::new(..) with embedding_table: None (defaulting to auto-resolution) plus split + value_columns, so it resolves whichever table is newest — a propagated one — and cannot scan its own origin.
symptom_spec.control: EXACT equality on the derived record's key_column (never != "_row_id", which passes vacuously on None, on "", and on any wrong-but-different name). A POSITIVE control asserting the origin fixture truly has no _row_id column, so the RED is attributable to the false provenance and not an unrelated missing column. A NEGATIVE control asserting a source whose origin key genuinely IS _row_id still records Some("_row_id") — failing any fix that blanket-drops or blanket-substitutes the literal. Resolution pinned against the record the producer RETURNS (resolve_embedding_table orders on app-supplied wall-clock created_at and can tie); the one deliberate shadowing case asserts the resolution landed on the propagated table so a tie fails loudly.

which_gate_missed: write-side provenance was recorded but never asserted — no test read back a derived table's catalog key_column. Every existing fixture (jammi-ai it/bench/gpu_capability, jammi-server) was itself _row_id-keyed, so a hardcoded "_row_id" was indistinguishable from a correct inherit: the two agree on every fixture in the repo. The defect was unobservable until a non-_row_id-keyed origin ran the propagate -> auto-resolve -> split/hydrate path end to end.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A jammi-cli integration test spawns its server on a port no other process can take, so the CLI's connect succeeds regardless of what else runs concurrently. The harness either holds the port until the server binds it, or lets the server bind an ephemeral port and reports back the one it got.
symptom_spec.observable: crates/jammi-cli/tests/it/server_harness.rs::free_port binds 127.0.0.1:0, reads local_addr().port(), then DROPS the listener and returns a bare u16 — releasing the port before the server binds it. Under the parallel workspace suite (cargo test --workspace runs many test binaries concurrently) another process can take the port in that window, and the CLI then fails: 'Error: Configuration error: connect to jammi endpoint: transport error'. Observed on cargo test --workspace --exclude jammi-python at channels::cli_channels_add_column_rejects_retype (flight port 40421); the same test passes in isolation (15/15) and on a re-run of the full suite, so it is load-dependent, not deterministic. Aggravated by wait_ready polling only the HEALTH port while the failure surfaced on the FLIGHT port — readiness is asserted on a different port than the one the client uses.
symptom_spec.control: A test that makes the race deterministic rather than probabilistic: hold a listener on the port between free_port and the server's bind (or spawn N harnesses concurrently under load) and assert the server still comes up — failing on the current release-then-rebind shape. A fix that only widens wait_ready's timeout must NOT pass: the failure is a stolen port, not a slow start.

which_gate_missed: no gate — the harness's own doc comment ACKNOWLEDGES the race and argues it away ('There is a small race between release and the server's bind, but on a CI host the kernel does not immediately re-hand the same port, so this is reliable for a test harness'), which is exactly the CLAUDE.md band-aid tell-sign 'a comment justifying why a wrong primitive is fine here'. The flake is load-dependent and self-clearing on retry, so it reads as infrastructure noise rather than a defect and no gate ever attributes it.
evidence_ref: DEFECT: crates/jammi-cli/tests/it/server_harness.rs::free_port (TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0") -> local_addr().port() -> listener dropped, bare u16 returned) and ::wait_ready (polls http_ok(health_port, "/readyz"), never the flight port the CLI connects to); consumed at ::TestServer spawn (flight_port/health_port both from free_port). OBSERVED: cargo test --workspace --exclude jammi-python, channels::cli_channels_add_column_rejects_retype, 'code=1 stderr=Error: Configuration error: connect to jammi endpoint: transport error' on grpc://127.0.0.1:40421; isolated re-run cargo test -p jammi-cli --test it = 15 passed 0 failed; full-suite re-run = 33 suites ok, 0 failed. PRE-EXISTING: server_harness.rs is byte-identical to origin/main@7f3477b (git diff --quiet clean); last touched by 3b8c097 (#131), long before this work. Surfaced while gating fix/key-column-provenance; demand-pulled and root-fixed in the v0.47.0 gap-closure batch. RESOLVED: the true class was a systemic serve-seam TOCTOU replicated ~14x across the server integration suite (root cause: the serve seam took a SocketAddr and bound it internally, forcing every harness to bind :0 -> read -> DROP -> rebind). Fix: eager-bind-and-expose -- OssServer::bind/AssembledChain::bind hold the listener from bind through serve (serve_with_incoming_shutdown), the CLI subprocess harness reads the server's reported ports (also fixing the wait_ready health-vs-flight aggravator), free_port and the self-exculpating comments deleted. Oracle crates/jammi-server/tests/it/serve_bind_race.rs (GREEN asserts an interposing TcpListener::bind -> AddrInUse before+during serve; RED control reconstructs the drop-then-return window); adversarial-audit confirmed non-vacuous.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: Every catalog key_column names a column of the source it points at, so a reader that follows the provenance (source.<key_column> = derived._row_id) can always resolve it. Where the engine cannot establish that at the write site, it should not leave the caller to discover it as a raw planner error from an unrelated verb much later.
symptom_spec.observable: ENGINE GAP, not caller error: import_embeddings offers key_column as a REQUIRED parameter, records it verbatim as the source-side provenance its own readers later scan, cannot validate it at that site, and does not warn. crates/jammi-ai/src/pipeline/import.rs::ImportPipeline::run enforces only non-emptiness and passes Some(key_column) to materialize_computed_embedding_table, which delegates to materialize_embedding_table and registers ResultTableKind::Model (crates/jammi-db/src/store/mod.rs); resolve_embedding_table filters kind = 'model' (crates/jammi-db/src/catalog/result_repo.rs), so the imported table IS auto-resolved, and filter_keys_by_split (crates/jammi-ai/src/pipeline/context_set.rs:490) / hydrate_value_columns (:545) interpolate the recorded name into SELECT arrow_cast("<name>",'Utf8') FROM <raw source>. This is the same false-provenance class as esc-025 reached through a public verb. It differs from esc-025 in DECIDABILITY, not in blame: propagate_embeddings held the source record's key_column at the call site and wrote the literal "_row_id" anyway (ground truth in hand, substituted), whereas at the import site source_id is a label stamped on a catalog row rather than a resolvable relation, so no ground truth is obtainable there.
symptom_spec.control: MUST FAIL TODAY (empirically verified, not asserted). Register a source keyed by doc_id with a split column and NO column named nope. import_embeddings(source_id="papers", key_column="nope", ...) -> the write SUCCEEDS: observed Ok((status "ready", key_column Some("nope"))). Then a reader that follows the provenance -- assemble_context with split = Some("split = 'train'") -- hard-fails with a raw planner error: observed Other("Context split: scan: Schema error: No field named nope. Valid fields are papers.public.src.doc_id, papers.public.src.split."). Passing shape for a fix: the failure is a typed provenance-mismatch error naming the table, the recorded key_column, and the source, instead of a raw DataFusion 'No field named nope'. A fix must NOT be accepted on a control that only asserts the write is rejected -- see the tenant-iso collision below.

which_gate_missed: no gate covers a write-side provenance value that is only decidable on the read side. The write site cannot check it (see the tenant-iso collision) and the read sites that CAN check it treat the mismatch as an ordinary planner failure rather than a provenance defect, so the recorded lie is never attributed to the verb that recorded it. esc-025 closed the two sites where the ground truth WAS in hand at the call site; this row is the residual where it is not.
evidence_ref: GAP: crates/jammi-ai/src/pipeline/import.rs::ImportPipeline::run (non-empty check only, then key_column: Some(key_column)); reachable from the gRPC surface via crates/jammi-ai/src/wire/embedding.rs::import_embeddings_from_proto -> crates/jammi-server/src/grpc/embedding.rs::import_embeddings, and from crates/jammi-python/src/database.rs. WHY NOT GUARDED AT THE WRITE SITE (empirically established, do not re-litigate without re-running it): guarding import with ensure_source_has_column BREAKS the per-RPC tenant-isolation HARD_BLOCK oracle. Probe result: tenant_isolation_oracle::every_case_isolation_holds FAILED with 'tenant A must import its own embedding table: Inference("Source 'import-src' not found")'; import_pipeline::import_pipeline_is_byte_identical_across_the_refactor and grpc_embedding::import_embeddings_rejects_dimension_mismatch_over_the_wire also FAILED, while grpc_embedding::import_embeddings_registers_a_ready_searchable_table_over_the_wire (which registers 'docs' carrying 'doc_id') PASSED. Both import paths import against a never-registered source (grep add_source in tenant_isolation_oracle.rs::assert_import_isolated = 0; in import_pipeline.rs = 0). The oracle states the premise VERBATIM at crates/jammi-server/tests/it/tenant_isolation_oracle.rs:1518-1523: 'import_embeddings writes a ready embedding table from precomputed vectors, stamping the catalog row with the scoped tenant. It resolves nothing at write time except the storage object it is handed, so the tenant boundary is the row it writes: a peer can neither resolve the source's embedding table nor read the imported row.' ensure_source_has_column resolves via crates/jammi-ai/src/session.rs::find_table_name, which reads the TENANT-SCOPED DataFusion context (self.inner.context()), so guarding at the write site would inject a tenant-scoped resolution into that HARD_BLOCK premise. CANDIDATE RESOLUTIONS: (c) LEADING -- validate on the READ side, where it IS decidable and where the source is already resolved: filter_keys_by_split (context_set.rs:490) and hydrate_value_columns (:545) already resolve the source and already fail there, so a typed provenance-mismatch error at that site replaces the raw 'No field named nope' with an honest one, at a decidable site, with ZERO tenant-iso collision; needs its own RED oracle, so it is a separate unit. (a) HEAVIER -- require a registered source for import and re-derive the tenant oracle's isolation argument, since import would then resolve a tenant-scoped relation at write time; this changes what the oracle proves and is a design decision, not a fix. (b) REJECTED -- guarding only when the source happens to resolve silently skips the check and re-opens the class. RESOLVED (v0.47.0 gap-closure) via the LEADING candidate (c): read-side validation -- filter_keys_by_split and hydrate_value_columns (context_set.rs) call ensure_source_has_column before the raw scan, emitting a typed JammiError::Schema naming table+column+source instead of the raw 'No field named X', at a decidable site with ZERO tenant-iso collision (the read path already resolves the source post-tenant-scope; oracle confirmed no new tenant surface). Oracle crates/jammi-ai/tests/it/context_set.rs::read_resolvers_reject_a_recorded_key_column_the_source_lacks (RED at base = raw 'No field named nope', GREEN = typed Schema); fix-verifier VERIFIED non-vacuous (exact assert on column=nope). The sibling context-set determinants value_columns (write-side) and split (read-side typed error) were closed in the same batch.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: Every serveable (encoder architecture x inference verb) pair that dispatches a GPU forward produces correct output on a real CUDA device, matching CPU up to reduction noise; a forward that errors surfaces rather than annotating empty.
symptom_spec.observable: ModernBERT Classification silently produced no output on a real A100 - candle CUDA matmul rejects the CLS narrow+squeeze 2-D row-stride operand its CPU matmul tolerates; infer per-row annotate semantics swallowed the error into empty scores. Latent because gpu_capability covered no ModernBert x Classification cell and the hermetic engine<->cookbook loop is CPU-only. Surfaced by the #310 GPU perf-baseline capture.
symptom_spec.control: Static coverage-completeness: parity cells declared under gpu_capability/ must cover every shipped (AnyEncoder variant x GPU-kernel verb) pair minus a reviewed structurally-impossible list; a shipped cell with no cell fails pre-merge. Plus a fail-loud arm (follow-up): a GPU forward erroring for every row surfaces, not empty.

which_gate_missed: no gate — the gated gpu_capability suite (crates/jammi-ai/tests/gpu_capability/) covered only a handful of (architecture, verb) cells with no completeness check over the SHIPPED (AnyEncoder architecture x GPU-dispatching ModelTask verb) surface, so an uncovered cell could not fail and the absence of a ModernBert x Classification parity test was invisible. CLOSED (the static half): ci/scripts/check_gpu_parity_matrix.py, wired as the 'Guard (GPU parity matrix)' job in .github/workflows/ci.yml, enumerates every SHIPPED cell and requires each to be COVERED (a `gpu-parity-cell` marker) / STRUCTURALLY_EXCLUDED / PENDING by name, plus a regression-guard oracle (crates/jammi-ai/tests/gpu_capability/classification_parity.rs, gpu-parity-cell: ModernBert x Classification). CLOSED (the fail-loud arm, PR #331): the runner propagates a systemic (non-OOM) forward Err instead of annotating it into empty output; build_error_batch/error_output deleted (crates/jammi-ai/src/inference/runner.rs). Regression guards: crates/jammi-ai/tests/it/e2e_inference.rs::{e2e_systemic_forward_failure_propagates_from_infer, e2e_systemic_forward_failure_propagates_from_embedding_pipeline, e2e_all_input_invalid_fails_loud_not_empty_ready_table}.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A CUDA artifact is promoted only after the release commit proves green on a real A100; a resource condition can never substitute for proof.
symptom_spec.observable: _gpu-prove-gate.yml treated RunPod capacity exhaustion (exit 75, SUPPLY_CONSTRAINT) as warn-and-pass: on a capacity outage the gate exited 0 and build->prove->promote promoted an UNPROVEN CUDA artifact (pypi-server-cuda wheel, server-cu12 image, release binaries), indistinguishable afterward from a proven one; the only trace was a transient workflow ::warning:: nobody re-reads. The esc-028 silent-success-on-resource-failure class, recurring at the release layer while the same drive eliminated it in-engine.
symptom_spec.control: Exit 75 fails the gate after bounded retry (3 attempts, 300s apart) with an ::error:: naming the condition and operator action; every promotion lane gates on the prove job's result == success, so a capacity outage blocks promotion until a green re-run. A real suite failure fails immediately with no retry.

which_gate_missed: none — the gate itself was the hole. No invariant asserted that a promotion gate fails closed; the esc-028 class abstraction (a resource condition producing successful-looking output) was applied to inference paths but not to the CI promotion path that gates them.
evidence_ref: PRE-FIX: .github/workflows/_gpu-prove-gate.yml@9fc04ab:36-39 (rc==75 -> ::warning:: + exit 0). FIX: .github/workflows/_gpu-prove-gate.yml (fail-closed bounded retry); promotion conditions verified at server-image.yml (build-and-push-cu12 if), _pypi-server.yml (publish if), release-binaries.yml (server-cu12 if).

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A process-global resource mutated by tests in more than one module is serialized by ONE mutex; every test that touches it contends on that mutex.
symptom_spec.observable: JAMMI_AUDIT_MASTER_KEY was guarded by two distinct `static ENV_LOCK: Mutex<()>` in the same test binary (audit/key_store.rs:57 and audit/signature.rs:154), each carrying the identical comment 'serialize the tests that touch it against each other'. A key_store test holding its lock could remove_var the key while a signature test holding the other lock had just set_var it, panicking with MasterKey("... is not set"); that panic then poisoned the signature lock and cascaded to the other 9 tests. Measured 1/30 full-binary runs under 4-way concurrency; invisible when the module is run in isolation.
symptom_spec.control: One lock declared beside the resource it guards (key_store::test_env), used by every module that mutates the var; poison recovered rather than propagated so a genuine failure surfaces as one failure, not a cascade that buries it. Structural check: exactly one `static ENV_LOCK` may exist for this variable.

which_gate_missed: no gate - test-infrastructure correctness is unasserted. Each lock reads as correct at its own call site; only the pair is wrong, and nothing compares declarations across modules.
evidence_ref: PRE-FIX: crates/jammi-db/src/audit/key_store.rs@9ad1131:57 and crates/jammi-db/src/audit/signature.rs@9ad1131:154 (two distinct statics). Base rate 1/30 concurrent full-binary runs; post-fix 0/60.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: The frozen base path of a linear computes identically whether or not that linear happens to be a LoRA target; a configured backbone_dtype means the same thing at every site.
symptom_spec.observable: MaybeLoraLinear::Frozen casts the input DOWN to the weight dtype and runs the matmul in the backbone dtype (wrapper.rs:31-38), while LoraLinear::forward allocates a fresh full-size F32 copy of the frozen weight on EVERY forward and runs the base matmul in F32 (lora_linear.rs:239-255). With lora_b initialised to zeros the LoRA delta is exactly 0, so both arms must be bit-identical for the same input at a reduced dtype - and are not. Consequence: backbone_dtype=bf16/f16 is inert on exactly the linears a LoRA run targets (with target_modules covering Wqkv/Wo/Wi that is every ModernBERT linear), buys no compute saving, and costs a per-forward full-weight materialisation.
symptom_spec.control: Zero-delta equality between the two arms at a reduced dtype, gated non-vacuously: assert lora_b.abs().sum()==0 before comparing (else a non-zero delta is mistaken for a dtype difference), require both outputs finite by a finite-COUNT check rather than any comparison bound (a NaN makes both `diff<eps` and `diff>eps` false), require both non-constant (max-min>0) so a zeroed matmul cannot pass, and keep an F32 positive control that must pass today - proving the harness discriminates dtype rather than reporting inequality everywhere.

which_gate_missed: no gate - no test compares the Frozen and Lora arms against each other at any dtype, and the reduced-dtype fine-tune path has no coverage at all.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-lora/src/lora_linear.rs@9ad1131:239-255 vs crates/jammi-lora/src/wrapper.rs@9ad1131:26-38. Reported as GH #345 with a different (incorrect) root cause.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A per-element dropout mask on a device-resident activation is produced on that device; it does not round-trip through the host, and it does not pin host-sized buffers in device memory for the backward pass.
symptom_spec.observable: LoraLinear::forward draws the mask with a single-threaded host scalar RNG loop over x.elem_count() (seeded.rs:127-135) and copies it device-ward via Tensor::from_vec on EVERY training forward (lora_linear.rs:278-284). For a ModernBERT-large-class encoder at batch 16 / seq 128 that is 0.98G host RNG draws and 3.92 GB of H2D per optimizer step (measured 0.31 s/step of pure host RNG on a fast desktop core, GPU idle throughout); at the shipped default max_seq_length=512 it is 1.96G draws and 7.84 GB. Because the mask is an operand of a mul whose other operand requires grad, every mask is additionally retained in device memory through backward - so the same quantity is a direct OOM contributor. Invisible to CPU-only tests, where the copy is free.
symptom_spec.control: Assert the per-forward host allocation is not proportional to batch*seq*in_features, and that mask residency does not scale with the number of LoRA sites on the tape. Pair with a determinism control: the mask stream must remain a pure function of (seed, qualified param name, position) so the fix cannot buy throughput by weakening reproducibility.

which_gate_missed: no gate - the hermetic suite is CPU-only, where a host-to-device copy has no cost and no distinct memory residency, so the entire failure mode is unobservable by construction.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-lora/src/seeded.rs@9ad1131:127-135, crates/jammi-lora/src/lora_linear.rs@9ad1131:278-284. Surfaced while triaging GH #345, which attributes the slowdown to backbone_dtype instead.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: Restoring a training run's dropout stream to a persisted position costs time independent of how far into the run that position is.
symptom_spec.observable: DropoutStream::restore_position rewinds to the origin and replays `position` draws one at a time (seeded.rs:145-152), and position advances by the full activation element count per forward (seeded.rs:133). After one realistic epoch of a large encoder that is ~1e11 draws per LoRA layer, times the layer count - so resume does not merely slow down, it fails to complete. The in-code comment justifies the replay as cheap on the grounds that 'the LoRA matrices are small', which describes the init draws, not the dropout draws it actually guards.
symptom_spec.control: Restore-to-position must be O(1) in position. Assert restore time is flat across positions spanning several orders of magnitude, and that the post-restore mask stream is byte-identical to an uninterrupted run's - so an O(1) skip cannot be bought by resuming onto a different stream.

which_gate_missed: no gate - resume is tested only at small positions, where an O(position) replay and an O(1) skip are indistinguishable.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-lora/src/seeded.rs@9ad1131:145-152 and :133. Found during phase-0.7 triage of GH #345; in no filed issue.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An encoder either honours every architecture field it accepts from a checkpoint's config, or refuses the checkpoint at load with a typed error naming the field it cannot honour. It never accepts a config it silently does not implement.
symptom_spec.observable: ModernBertConfig deserializes local_attention, local_rope_theta and global_attn_every_n_layers (modernbert.rs:83-88) and no forward or builder path reads them again: every layer builds its RoPE table from global_rope_theta (modernbert.rs:567-572) and attention adds only the padding mask (modernbert.rs:206-214). For any checkpoint with global_attn_every_n_layers != 1 - which includes the ModernBERT-large family at 3 - two of every three layers compute full global attention with the wrong RoPE base, i.e. a different function than the checkpoint specifies, with no error and no warning. The port's own doc comment declares its valid domain as global_attn_every_n_layers == 1 (modernbert.rs:63-70) and nothing enforces it.
symptom_spec.control: Causal-isolation on a local layer using a fixture that can express the symptom (multi-layer, global_attn_every_n_layers=3, window narrower than the sequence, no padding so the additive pad mask cannot be confused for the band): perturbing a token outside the window must leave an in-window position's local-layer state unchanged. Non-vacuous only with three controls in the same test - an in-window position MUST change (proves the perturbation propagates), the same position on a GLOBAL layer MUST change (proves the band is selective, not a broken forward), and both states asserted finite by a finite-COUNT check, since a -inf mask row that softmaxes to NaN passes any comparison-based 'unchanged' assertion.

which_gate_missed: no gate - every ModernBERT fixture in-tree is num_hidden_layers=1 / global_attn_every_n_layers=1, so layer 0 is global under both semantics and no fixture can express the divergence. The coverage hole and the defect share a root: the fixture set was built from the port's assumed domain.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-encoders/src/modernbert.rs@9ad1131:83-88, :206-214, :567-572; blind fixtures at tests/fixtures/tiny_modernbert/config.json and cookbook/fixtures/tiny_modernbert_{classifier,ner}/config.json. Documented in GH #350, which proposes no change.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A metric that was never measured never drives checkpoint selection, early stopping, or a reported result. An empty measurement domain is refused, not scored.
symptom_spec.observable: evaluate() returns Ok(0.0) for an empty validation loader (trainer.rs:1627-1629). Under the DEFAULT early_stopping_metric=ValLoss this makes monitor_loss 0.0 every epoch: epoch 0 wins 0.0 < f64::MAX and writes checkpoint_best (trainer.rs:391, :586-589), every later epoch fails 0.0 < 0.0 and increments patience (:591-592), the loop breaks at patience+1 epochs, the epoch-0 checkpoint is reloaded as the PUBLISHED adapter (:625-628), and final_loss is reported as 0.0 (:657, :667). So a run silently ships an essentially untrained adapter and reports a perfect loss. Reachable two ways: explicit validation_fraction=0.0, and - not reported in the issue - the DEFAULT validation_fraction=0.1 on any dataset where round(N*0.1)==0, i.e. fewer than 5 rows.
symptom_spec.control: Assert the run completes its full epoch horizon, that the returned adapter is NOT bit-equal to the end-of-epoch-0 weights across ALL trainable params (exact equality, not a norm, so a partial restore cannot pass), and that final_loss is finite AND strictly positive - a bare `!= 0.0` is vacuous against NaN, which also silently satisfies `monitor < best` never firing, the same collapse in another mask. Positive control in the same test: the identical run with a non-empty validation split must train the full horizon and return a finite decreasing monitored loss.

which_gate_missed: no gate - validate() range-checks validation_fraction in [0.0,1.0) (fine_tune.rs:441-450) with no cross-field rule against ValLoss, and no test runs the trainer with an empty validation split.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/trainer.rs@9ad1131:1627-1629, :391, :586-592, :625-628, :657, :667; crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/data.rs@9ad1131:465. Reported as GH #347, whose FIRST stated root cause is refuted (proto3 explicit presence already carries a set 0.0).

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: A registered directory source either reads its rows or fails with a typed error naming why; it never resolves to an empty, columnless table that reports no problem.
symptom_spec.observable: FileFormat::Json is documented as newline-delimited JSON (source/mod.rs:41-42) and DataFusion's JsonFormat reads .jsonl content, but create_listing_table hardcodes the listing extension to '.json' (source/file_format.rs:56-64). A directory of .jsonl files registered as Json therefore matches zero objects and resolves with no usable schema or rows, with no diagnostic naming the extension mismatch. The file_extension override that would rescue it exists on SourceConnection (mod.rs:85-87) but is unreachable from the CLI, which exposes only name/url/format (commands/sources.rs:25-27).
symptom_spec.control: Row-count equality against a matched positive control in the same test: byte-identical rows written to .json files in a sibling directory, registered identically, must return exactly N - proving the reader, schema inference and count path all work and that only extension routing differs. Assert the returned schema's field NAMES equal the expected set, so an inferred-empty or all-null schema cannot pass as a read; and require any surfaced error to be a typed error naming the extension - a bare Ok(0 rows) and an opaque downstream 'column not found' both count as the bad path.

which_gate_missed: no gate - no test registers a directory source whose file extension differs from the format's default, so the silent-empty path is never exercised.
evidence_ref: crates/jammi-db/src/source/file_format.rs@9ad1131:56-64, crates/jammi-db/src/source/mod.rs@9ad1131:41-42 and :85-87, crates/jammi-cli/src/commands/sources.rs@9ad1131:25-27. Reported as GH #346, which frames it as a missing format spelling.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: An operator that cannot participate in backward fails loudly when a gradient is required through it; it never silently returns a zero/absent gradient that reads as successful training.
symptom_spec.observable: candle's apply_op1_no_bwd constructs its result with BackpropOp::none() (candle-core custom_op.rs:156-159), so backward through such a tensor does not raise BackwardNotSupported - it stops traversing. Two operators the engine reaches for take this path: candle_nn::ops::softmax_last_dim (candle-nn ops.rs:437-439), already called at jammi-encoders/src/htsat_audio.rs:632, jammi-encoders/src/clip_text.rs:150 and jammi-ai/src/model/backend/open_clip_vit.rs:169; and QMatMul (candle-core quantized/mod.rs:1023), the natural entry point for quantized fine-tuning. Any trainable parameter placed upstream of one of these receives no gradient while the loss still decreases plausibly from the parameters that remain connected.
symptom_spec.control: A gradient-reachability assertion rather than a loss-decreases assertion: for every trainable Var, require a non-None, non-zero gradient after one backward on a non-degenerate batch. A test that only checks the loss went down cannot distinguish a partially-connected graph from a fully-connected one.

which_gate_missed: no gate - nothing asserts that every registered trainable Var actually receives a gradient. The three current call sites are correct only incidentally: neither the CLIP nor the HTSAT tower is LoRA-wrapped, so the truncation sits upstream of every Var.
evidence_ref: candle-core-0.11.0/src/custom_op.rs:156-159; candle-nn-0.11.0/src/ops.rs:437-439; candle-core-0.11.0/src/quantized/mod.rs:1023; call sites as listed. Latent, not live. Recorded as GH #351 context.

symptom_spec.intended_behavior: K3's standardization oracles must assert the distributional property K3 actually guarantees - that data-space standardization keeps the served fit/dispersion bounded across training trajectories - so they pass on unmodified code for EVERY seed, not for the one seed the default happens to land on.
symptom_spec.observable: On unmodified code, varying ONLY FineTuneConfig.seed (the sole randomness source: the LoRA-A Kaiming draw, lora.rs:56 -> lora_linear.rs:131; features() is a fixed LCG) over a pinned 12-seed set: ft_quantile_scale_robust_on_high_variance_target (trainer.rs:3625) FAILS on >=4 of 12 seeds, and crps_served_output_preserved_within_tolerance_z_vs_raw (trainer.rs:3829) shows row-0 served-sigma gaps of 2.48/4.48/1.31/2.12 against sigma_tol=2.0 across sampled seeds. The wrong state is the pass RATE itself: 8/12 on correct code where the required state is 12/12 (or an explicitly aggregated statistic with stated margin). The rewritten test must assert the sweep outcome, not a single default-seed run.
symptom_spec.control: Two-sided over the SAME pinned seed set. (1) Anti-relaxation: the rewritten distributional test must go RED on ALL seeds under each K3-breaking mutant: (i) TargetScaler neutralized to identity; (ii) raw-space targets with the loss divided by sigma_y (the K3-forbidden alternative); (iii) served sigma built with gaussian_scaled(1.0) instead of gaussian_scaled(sigma_y) (trainer.rs:3214-3217, the ~19x under-dispersion). A rewrite under which mutant (iii) passes is a relaxation hiding a regression. Bounds stay small relative to sigma_y (mean <= ~0.3*sigma_y, sigma <= ~0.5*sigma_y). (2) Non-finite robustness: every per-seed measurement is is_finite()-asserted before aggregation and a non-finite seed COUNTS AS FAILING; no assertion form that NaN satisfies; pass criterion is an explicit count of seeds positively satisfying a finite bound.

provenance: issue #352 outstanding finding 6; phase-0.7 triage 2026-08-23; fix must land in its own commit with the pre-change multi-seed run attached, never inside a perf change
